seo.description: Plan your trip to Oujda: explore the authentic medina of Oujda, the 14 km Blue Pearl beach of Saïdia, parks, local food, hotels & riads, a 3-day itinerary, and practical tips for eastern Morocco.
seo.og_title: Oujda Travel Guide | Medina, Beaches & Day Trips | MoroccoTripMap
seo.og_description: Authentic medina, Mediterranean beaches, parks and day trips from Oujda to Saïdia, all in one practical guide.

hero_subtitle: Eastern Morocco’s cultural capital: medina alleys, palm parks, and the Blue Pearl beach of Saïdia nearby.

overview.title: Welcome to the Capital of the Oriental
overview.p1: Oujda is Morocco’s eastern gateway, a thousand-year-old city of living medina streets, Gharnati music and everyday markets that still feel local. Just 60 km north, Saïdia – the Blue Pearl – stretches along 14 kilometres of fine Mediterranean sand, with a modern marina and calm family-friendly waters.
overview.p2: Whether you wander the medina through Bab Sidi Abdelwahab, sip barida in a shaded park, or spend a day on Saïdia’s beach and return for evening karan, Oujda offers a rare mix of authentic city life and easy seaside escape without the crowds of the classic imperial circuit.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Oujda
places.subtitle: Historic gates, green parks, the Great Mosque and the long Mediterranean beach you cannot miss.

medina.title: Medina of Oujda & Bab Sidi Abdelwahab
medina.desc: A compact, authentic medina with spice stalls, leather workshops and far fewer touts than the big tourist cities.

mosque.title: Grande Mosquée (Al Kabir)
mosque.desc: The city’s oldest mosque, founded in the Marinid era, with its elegant minaret and the famous three fountains.

parc.title: Parc Lalla Aicha
parc.desc: Oujda’s green lung: shaded paths, fountains and a favourite family gathering place designed in the 1930s.

dar_sebti.title: Dar Sebti
dar_sebti.desc: A restored 20th-century palace that hosts cultural events and Gharnati music performances.

place.title: Place du 16 Août & Clock Tower
place.desc: The lively central square with its 1920s art-deco clock tower and cafés ideal for people-watching.

sidi_yahya.title: Sidi Yahya Oasis
sidi_yahya.desc: A palm-fringed oasis with thermal springs a short drive east of the city, quiet and local.

saidia_beach.title: Plage de Saïdia
saidia_beach.desc: Fourteen kilometres of golden sand and calm turquoise water, Morocco’s longest continuous Mediterranean beach.

marina.title: Marina de Saïdia
marina.desc: A large marina with restaurants, evening promenades and water-sport bases right on the seafront.

zegzel.title: Vallée de Zegzel & Beni Snassen
zegzel.desc: Green valleys, prehistoric caves and mountain scenery less than an hour from Oujda.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan to discover the medina, parks and the Blue Pearl without rushing.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Enter through Bab Sidi Abdelwahab while the light is soft. Walk the spice and leather souks, admire the exterior of the Grande Mosquée and the three fountains.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Continue to Parc Lalla Aicha for shade and local life, then visit Dar Sebti if open for cultural events or architecture.
detailed_itinerary.day1_e: Evening — Place du 16 Août & Local Food
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Watch the square come alive at dusk. Try karan and barida or grilled meats in a neighbourhood café.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Take a grand taxi or hire a driver (about 1 hour). Arrive at the beach, choose a quiet stretch of sand and enjoy the Mediterranean.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Stroll the marina, rent a paddleboard or jet-ski if you wish, and have a late seafood lunch by the water.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Walk the seafront as the light turns gold, then return to Oujda or stay overnight in a Saïdia resort.
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Zegzel Valley or Sidi Yahya
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Head to the Beni Snassen mountains and Zegzel caves, or spend a quieter morning at Sidi Yahya oasis.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Back in Oujda, revisit a favourite souk lane, buy regional textiles or citrus products, or enjoy a traditional hammam.
detailed_itinerary.day3_e: Evening — Last Night in the Oriental
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: A final mint tea on a terrace or a relaxed dinner of local specialities before departure.

stays.title: Where to Stay in Oujda? Our Favourites
stays.subtitle: Central riads and practical hotels in Oujda, or beach resorts in Saïdia for a seaside stay.

card1.name: Riad Dar Al Fassia
card1.desc: A well-reviewed traditional riad in Oujda with warm hospitality and a convenient location near the centre.

card2.name: Riad ADAHAB
card2.desc: Intimate riad with garden, shared lounge and authentic Moroccan atmosphere a short walk from key sights.

card3.name: Mediterrania Saïdia Resorts
card3.desc: Modern beachfront complexes with pools, restaurants and direct access to the long sandy beach.

card4.name: Hotels near Place du 16 Août
card4.desc: Comfortable mid-range hotels ideal for exploring the medina and parks on foot.

eat.title: Best Places to Eat in Oujda
eat.subtitle: Local specialities, street food and fresh seafood by the sea

karan.title: Karan & Barida
karan.desc: The iconic chickpea gratin served hot with a glass of iced barida (lemonade) – the taste of Oujda street life.

medina_food.title: Souk Grills & Snails
medina_food.desc: Simple stalls serving grilled meats, snails and fresh bread in the heart of the medina.

seafood.title: Fresh Fish at the Marina
seafood.desc: Grilled fish, calamari and Mediterranean salads with a view of the boats.

traditional.title: Regional Tagines & Pastilla
traditional.desc: Home-style Moroccan dishes with an Oriental touch, often found in family-run restaurants.

cafe.title: City Cafés
cafe.desc: Terraces for mint tea, strong coffee and watching the daily rhythm of the square.

resort.title: Beachfront Restaurants
resort.desc: Relaxed dining with sea views, perfect after a day on the sand.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.desc: Walking works well in the medina and central Oujda. For Saïdia use grand taxis (shared or private). Agree the price or insist on the meter for petit taxis in town.

bargain.title: Souk Bargaining
bargain.desc: Prices start lower than in major tourist centres. Negotiate with a smile; starting around 60 % of the asking price is usually fair.

water.title: Stay Hydrated & Sun-Safe
water.desc: Summers are hot. Carry bottled water, wear a hat and use sunscreen, especially on Saïdia beach.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Oujda
daytrips.subtitle: Easy escapes by grand taxi or private driver to beaches, mountains and citrus country.

saidia.title: Saïdia Beach Day
saidia.desc: The classic 60 km trip to 14 km of golden sand, marina and calm Mediterranean water.

zegzel.title: Vallée de Zegzel & Caves
zegzel.desc: Green valleys, prehistoric caves and mountain air in the Beni Snassen range.

berkane.title: Berkane & Citrus Country
berkane.desc: Agricultural town famous for oranges and a lively local market atmosphere.

raselma.title: Cap de l’Eau (Ras El Ma)
raselma.desc: Dramatic cliffs, fishing village and panoramic views toward the Chafarinas Islands.

q1.question: How many days should I spend in Oujda?
q1.answer: 3 to 5 days lets you explore the medina and parks of Oujda, enjoy a full beach day (or overnight) in Saïdia, and fit in one nature excursion to Zegzel or Sidi Yahya.

q2.question: Is Oujda safe for international tourists?
q2.answer: Yes, the area is generally calm and welcoming. As in any city, keep an eye on belongings in crowded markets and agree taxi prices in advance. The border zone itself is not a tourist area.

q3.question: What currency is used and can I pay by credit card?
q3.answer: Morocco uses the Moroccan Dirham (MAD). Cards work in larger hotels and some restaurants, but cash is essential for taxis, medina shops, street food and most small businesses.

q4.question: How do I get from Oujda-Angad Airport to the city or Saïdia?
q4.answer: Oujda-Angad (OUD) is about 15 km from central Oujda. Official taxis and pre-booked transfers are available. To Saïdia count roughly 1 hour by grand taxi or private transfer.
